name: The Thing From The Future
description:
The Thing from the Future is a futures-oriented ideation game in which prompts are combined to imagine an artefact from a possible future. Constraints commonly describe elements such as the type of future, the time horizon, the kind of object and an emotional or thematic quality.

The random combination pushes participants away from familiar predictions and toward a wider range of future possibilities.
whenToUse: Use the method when a group needs to expand its imagination of possible futures, begin a futures workshop or generate speculative artefacts quickly.
steps: Establish the issue or domain being explored.
Generate or draw a set of future-oriented prompts.
Combine prompts to create an unusual design constraint.
Individually or collaboratively imagine an artefact responding to it.
Sketch and describe how the artefact works.
Explain what future conditions would make the artefact meaningful.
Compare the assumptions and worlds implied by different artefacts.
lookOutFor: The artefact is a doorway into discussing a future, not simply an unusual product-design exercise.
Randomness can produce superficial ideas unless participants develop the surrounding social context.

resources.citation: Candy, S. & Watson, J. (2015). *The Thing from the Future*. Situation Lab.
